content.text: Prop firm rules change often. This guide reflects the firm's published rules when it was last updated (see the date above). Always confirm current rules on the firm's official site before you trade your evaluation.

The FTMO Challenge is one of the best-known funded programs in the industry, and passing it means something. But knowing exactly how to pass it is not as obvious as it seems, even for experienced futures traders.

The short answer: you pass the FTMO evaluation by treating it less like a performance challenge and more like a rule compliance challenge. Most traders who fail have workable strategies — they fail because they blow the max daily loss after a frustrating session, misread how the max loss works on their challenge type, or take one oversized trade that destroys a week of careful progress.

This guide covers the FTMO rules you need to know (verified Nov 22, 2026), the math behind the 1-Step Best Day Rule, the behavioral patterns that kill most attempts, and the daily habits of traders who pass on their first or second try.
FTMO Evaluation: 2-Step vs 1-Step
FTMO offers two paths. The classic 2-Step Challenge has a Challenge phase and a Verification phase. The 1-Step challenge has a single phase with tighter loss limits and a Best Day Rule:

On a $100,000 2-Step account: the Challenge requires $10,000 in profit and the Verification $5,000. In both phases the max daily loss is $5,000 — 5% of the initial balance, measured from your balance at the start of each day — and the max loss is $10,000, so your floor sits at $90,000. You need at least 4 trading days per phase, and there is no time limit.

Last verified Nov 22, 2026 from FTMO's rules pages and 2026 rule guides. Rules vary by account size, challenge type and purchase date. Confirm the current trading objectives with FTMO before you start. For a one-page summary, see our FTMO rules hub.
The FTMO Best Day Rule (1-Step) — and Why the 2-Step Has No Consistency Rule

Much of the content online still says FTMO has a 30% consistency rule. It doesn't. The standard 2-Step Challenge has no consistency rule. The 1-Step challenge has a Best Day Rule: no single day can account for more than 50% of your total profit.
How the Best Day Rule Is Calculated
The formula is simple: Best Day Profit ÷ Total Profit ≤ 50%.

items: Total profit: $6,000
Your single best day: $2,400
Best-day share: $2,400 ÷ $6,000 = 40% — within the rule
Total profit: $6,000
Your single best day: $3,300
Best-day share: $3,300 ÷ $6,000 = 55% — breaks the 50% rule

content.text: The deceptive part: the ratio changes every day. With a $3,300 best day you would need more than $6,600 in total profit to bring it down to 50%. The only way to know where you stand is to track it after every session. Check FTMO's rules for exactly how the Best Day Rule is applied to your account.

On a 1-Step challenge, check your best-day share every single day. If a strong day pushes it above 40%, keep your size normal and stop chasing another big day — let your total catch up. Zentrade lets you set a 50% consistency threshold on the account and shows your best-day share live.
Common FTMO Failure Patterns — And How to Avoid Them
Failure Pattern 1: Revenge Trading After the Daily Loss

The max daily loss on FTMO ($5,000 on a $100,000 2-Step account) is a hard stop. Many traders hit 80% of their daily limit early in the session, feel frustrated, and take one more trade — the one that crosses the line. The solution is a personal daily loss limit set below FTMO's limit: if your rule is to stop at -$3,500, you keep a $1,500 buffer before the hard limit. When you hit your personal limit, you close the platform.
Failure Pattern 2: The Big Day Trap

A trader has an exceptional day — $4,000 in profit on a $100,000 account. They feel invincible. The next day they double their position size, confident the streak will continue. Instead, they give back $3,500 in two trades. This pattern — exceptional day followed by an oversized loss — is one of the most common account-ending sequences. Journal your best days specifically and treat the next session as high-risk.
Failure Pattern 3: Rushing Against a Deadline That Doesn't Exist

Traders who feel they are running out of time start taking lower-quality setups to reach the profit target faster. The result is more losses, more variance and a higher chance of hitting a loss limit. FTMO removed the old 30/60-day limits: there is no time limit on the challenge. Trade your plan, not the calendar.
Failure Pattern 4: Misreading How Your Max Loss Works

On the 2-Step challenge the 10% max loss is static: on a $100,000 account your floor stays at $90,000 no matter how much you make, so every dollar of profit adds to your cushion. On the 1-Step challenge the max loss trails your end-of-day balance, so your floor rises after profitable days and your cushion does not grow the same way. Know which one you bought — the position sizing math is different.
How to Structure Your Trading Plan for the FTMO Evaluation
Passing FTMO is not about trading more — it is about trading consistently within a defined structure. Here is the framework that the most successful FTMO traders use:

items: Define your maximum position size — not based on what you want to earn, but on what keeps you within the daily loss limit with three consecutive losing trades
Set a personal daily loss limit — 60-70% of FTMO's limit (e.g., $3,000-$3,500 instead of $5,000 on a $100,000 2-Step account)
Set a daily profit target — once you hit it, stop trading. It prevents the Big Day Trap and, on the 1-Step, keeps your best-day share in check
Define the hours you trade — for US index futures, the most liquid windows are usually 8:30-11:00 AM ET and 1:30-3:30 PM ET. Stick to your windows
Journal every trade immediately — emotional state, rationale, compliance with plan
Check your numbers every morning — distance to the daily and max loss, and your best-day share if you are on the 1-Step
Take at least one full day off per week — fatigue is a direct cause of rule violations

content.text: FTMO vs. Other Prop Firms: Is the Two-Phase Process Worth It?
FTMO's 2-Step structure asks for more than a single-phase evaluation like Apex Trader Funding or the Topstep Trading Combine. So why would a trader choose FTMO?

items: Brand recognition: FTMO is one of the best-known prop firms worldwide
No time limit: the old 30/60-day limits were removed
No consistency rule on the 2-Step: a big day does not count against you
Static max loss on the 2-Step: your floor does not trail your profits, so your cushion grows as you win

FTMO Evaluation: Frequently Asked Questions

faqItems.q: How long does the FTMO evaluation take?
faqItems.a: There is no time limit: FTMO removed the old 30/60-day limits. On the 2-Step challenge you need at least 4 trading days per phase. How long it takes depends on your strategy and how patiently you build toward the profit target.

faqItems.q: What happens if I fail the FTMO Challenge?
faqItems.a: If you break a loss rule, the challenge ends and you need a new one to try again. Check FTMO's site for current retry options and prices.

faqItems.q: Can I trade futures on FTMO?
faqItems.a: FTMO lists the instruments available for each account type on its site. Before you buy, check that the contracts you trade (for example ES, NQ or GC) are available and how they are offered.

faqItems.q: Does FTMO have a consistency rule?
faqItems.a: The standard 2-Step FTMO Challenge has no consistency rule. The 1-Step challenge has a Best Day Rule: no single day can account for more than 50% of your total profit. Zentrade calculates your best day's share of profit in real time; set your threshold to 50%.

faqItems.q: How is the FTMO max daily loss calculated?
faqItems.a: On the 2-Step challenge the maximum daily loss is 5% of the initial account balance (for example $5,000 on a $100,000 account), measured from the balance at the start of each day; on the 1-Step challenge it is 3%. Check FTMO's rules for how open positions count.

faqItems.q: Is the FTMO max loss trailing or static?
faqItems.a: It depends on the challenge. On the 2-Step the 10% max loss is static: a $100,000 account has a $90,000 floor that never moves. On the 1-Step the max loss trails your end-of-day balance, so the floor rises after profitable days.
